encounters.cc: Brought by her daughter because of worsening memory loss and functional decline over the past 2 years.

lines: Brought by her daughter because of worsening memory loss and functional decline over the past 2 years.
She frequently misplaces household items, repeats the same questions during conversations, and occasionally becomes disoriented in familiar places.
She has also developed irritability and difficulty managing daily finances.
Her past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, controlled with medications.
Family history is notable for a sibling who developed similar symptoms in late adulthood.
She does not drink alcohol or use illicit substances.
On examination, she is alert but unable to recall three objects after five minutes and struggles with clock-drawing and serial subtraction tasks.
Motor and sensory exams are normal, and gait is steady.
Basic laboratory studies including thyroid function and vitamin B12 are within normal limits.
MRI of the brain shows generalized cortical atrophy, most prominent in the temporal and parietal lobes.

encounters.cc: Progressive difficulty reading and recognizing faces over the past six months with central vision blurriness.

lines: Progressive difficulty reading and recognizing faces over the past six months with central vision blurriness.

The patient is a 71-year-old female with a history of Alzheimer disease diagnosed in January 2020 who presents to the ophthalmology clinic complaining of progressive difficulty reading and recognizing faces over the past six months.
She reports that her central vision is increasingly blurry and that when looking at a grid pattern, the lines appear wavy.
She denies any pain or redness in her eyes.
Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with lisinopril, and hypercholesterolemia, managed with atorvastatin.
She has a 30-pack-year smoking history but quit 10 years ago.
On physical examination, her visual acuity is 20/60 in both eyes.
The anterior segment and pupillary responses are normal.
Fundoscopic examination reveals bilateral drusen and pigmentary changes in the macula.
No hemorrhages or exudates are noted.

encounters.cc: Bilateral lower extremity swelling that has progressively worsened over the past two weeks with 5-pound weight gain.

lines: Bilateral lower extremity swelling that has progressively worsened over the past two weeks with 5-pound weight gain.

This 72-year-old female with Alzheimer disease diagnosed in 2020 and dry age-related macular degeneration diagnosed in 2021 returns to the Internal Medicine clinic complaining of bilateral lower extremity swelling that has progressively worsened over the past two weeks.
She denies any chest pain, dyspnea, orthopnea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea.
She reports a weight gain of 5 pounds during this period.
Her medications include amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide, and atorvastatin.
Smoking: 40 pack-year history; quit 10 years ago but relapsed and currently smokes 1 pack per day.
On physical examination, her blood pressure is 142/88 mmHg, heart rate is 78 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute.
Cardiac examination reveals a regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Lung fields are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
There is 2+ pitting edema up to the mid-shins bilaterally.

encounters.cc: Several episodes of dizziness and near-syncope occurring when using her left arm for tasks like combing hair or carrying groceries.

lines: Several episodes of dizziness and near-syncope occurring when using her left arm for tasks like combing hair or carrying groceries.

The patient with Alzheimer disease, hypertension, and dry age-related macular degeneration presents with dizziness and near-syncope that occur when using her left arm for tasks like combing her hair or carrying groceries, as well as left arm easily fatigued with activity.
She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia.
She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years
On examination, her blood pressure is 144/90 mm Hg in the right arm and 114/72 mm Hg in the left
The left radial pulse is decreased compared to the right, and femoral pulse is normal bilaterally.

encounters.cc: Increasing difficulty in initiating movements, stiffness in her arms and legs, and a resting tremor in her right hand over 2 months.

lines: Increasing difficulty in initiating movements, stiffness in her arms and legs, and a resting tremor in her right hand over 2 months.
Patient is a 74-year-old female with chronic schizophrenia and Alzheimer disease diagnosed in 2020.
She returns to the Psychiatry clinic with a 2-month history of increasing difficulty in initiating movements, stiffness in her arms and legs, and a resting tremor in her right hand.
She has been stable on her antipsychotic medication for years.
Her family notes that she has become less expressive and her voice has softened.
Her most recent medication regimen includes risperidone 4 mg daily, started 6 months ago.
Her other medications include lisinopril for hypertension and atorvastatin for hyperlipidemia.
Smoking: 40 pack-year history; quit 10 years ago but relapsed and currently smokes 1 pack per day.
On examination, she exhibits a shuffling gait, bilateral cogwheel rigidity, and bradykinesia.
There is no evidence of a pill-rolling tremor.

encounters.cc: Repetitive chewing motions and occasional tongue protrusion observed by her daughter over the past 6 months.

lines: Repetitive chewing motions and occasional tongue protrusion observed by her daughter over the past 6 months.

The patient is a 74-year-old with chronic schizophrenia who returns to the psychiatry clinic with her daughter following a January 2024 visit for movement side effects, and her daughter reports that over the past 6 months, her mother has developed repetitive chewing motions and occasional tongue protrusion.
The patient has been stable on her antipsychotic medication for 10 years.
She takes risperidone 4 mg daily, metformin for type 2 diabetes, and atorvastatin for hyperlipidemia.
Smoking: 40 pack-year history; quit 10 years ago but relapsed and currently smokes 1 pack per day.
Her vital signs are within normal limits
On examination, the patient exhibits involuntary, rhythmic movements of her jaw and tongue.
She also has intermittent grimacing and blinking.
There is no evidence of rigidity, tremor, or bradykinesia.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset of right arm weakness and difficulty speaking that resolved completely within 45 minutes.

lines: Sudden onset of right arm weakness and difficulty speaking that resolved completely within 45 minutes.
This 75-year-old female with Alzheimer disease and subclavian steal syndrome presents with sudden onset of right arm weakness and difficulty speaking that resolved completely within 45 minutes.
She denies any headache, trauma, or loss of consciousness.
- Oculogyric crisis due to antipsychotic medication (diagnosed 2024-07-15)
Her medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin.
Smoking: 40 pack-year history; quit 10 years ago but relapsed and currently smokes 1 pack per day.
Her blood pressure is 155/90 mmHg, heart rate is 78 bpm
Her neurological examination is now normal
An ECG shows normal sinus rhythm without evidence of atrial fibrillation.

encounters.cc: Sudden episode of syncope preceded by brief chest pain and shortness of breath after climbing stairs.

lines: Sudden episode of syncope preceded by brief chest pain and shortness of breath after climbing stairs.
The patient with chronic schizophrenia, Alzheimer disease, and prior TIA presents acutely.
She reports that earlier in the day, she experienced brief chest pain and shortness of breath after climbing a flight of stairs.
- Oculogyric crisis due to antipsychotic medication (diagnosed 2024-07-15)
Her medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin.
Smoking: 40 pack-year history; quit 10 years ago but relapsed and currently smokes 1 pack per day.
Her blood pressure is 85/50 mmHg, heart rate is 120 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 28 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 88% on room air.
The patient's blood pressure drops further to 75/40 mmHg despite fluid resuscitation.
On examination, she appears diaphoretic and in distress.
Lung auscultation reveals clear breath sounds bilaterally.
Cardiac examination shows tachycardia without murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Extremities are cool to touch, and there is no peripheral edema.
A bedside echocardiogram demonstrates right ventricular dilation with hypokinesis of the right ventricular free wall.
An electrocardiogram shows sinus tachycardia and a S1Q3T3 pattern.
